overview: This table defines what each binding vow does in battle and which message describes that effect.
description: Concrete binding-vow effects: an effect-type discriminator, type-dependent numeric parameters, and the battle-text ID used to describe the effect in UI.

Id.simple: The name the game uses to attach this effect to a binding vow.
Id.technical: FName row key in BindingVowsEffectDataTable; the export writes it as ID and declares Id as ImportKeyField. GameBindingVows_GetEffectRows scans BindingVowsDataTables, uses the first table containing the vow ID, skips None effect IDs, and for each ID resolves the first matching row in BindingVowsEffectDataTables; later table matches are ignored. DTM_FindBindingVowsEffectRow applies the same first-table precedence when the selection UI resolves the ordered effect IDs directly. Resolved row pointers are also held transiently in FGameCharacterBindingVowsEffectState::Effect for status checks.

EffectType.simple: Choose what this vow changes or switches on, such as health, movement, attack power, Cursed Energy, or mission rewards.
EffectType.technical: EGameBindingVowsEffectType (uint8): None=0, behavior enumerators 1-80, Invalid=255; the row constructor defaults to None. GameBindingVows_GetEffectRowsOfType filters joined rows by this value, status code switches on it, and GameBattleSystems_B uses it for failed/dead-vow checks. It also drives the widget's hit-point/movement/attack/cursed-energy/other category (together with the paired buff/debuff slot), while MissionOrder and MissionTask exclusion arrays use it to reject PvE vow candidates. Interpretation of EffectValue is type-specific; several flag-only types use EffectType presence with 0/0 values.

EffectValue.simple: These numbers set the effect's strength, chance, or required condition. A bigger number can make the change stronger, more likely, or harder to reach.
EffectValue.technical: TArray<float>. The sole export shard has 239 rows and every row has exactly two finite values. [0] is polymorphic: GameBindingVows_SumEffectRate treats each value as a raw multiplier and accumulates Value-1; GameBindingVows_SumEffectValue sums raw [0] (or takes a max floored at 0); ForceGaugeMax adds [0] to an int base and clamps nonnegative results to at least 1; battle-log vows store [0] as State.Required; HitPointOnce treats [0] as a maximum-HP ratio; elapsed-time types use [0] with GetBattleElapsedTime; and chance types pass int32([0]*100) out of 100 to RollChance kind 2. [1] is the applied magnitude/multiplier for the relevant types: HitPointWhenJustGuard adds HitPointMax*[1], HitPointOnce adds int32([1]*HitPointMax), RateAtValue helpers add [1]-1 after the [0] threshold test, SendAttackDamageEveryWithTime multiplies the rate by [1] for each elapsed/[0] interval, and DeadKillWithTime/DeadCursedEnergyLevelWithTime compare [1] after their [0] time limit is reached. Many simple or flag-only types use only [0] or store 0/0, so zero in an unused slot is a placeholder rather than a universal value. Runtime helpers index the array without bounds checks; the selection UI requires EffectValue.Num()>=2 before passing both entries to text parameters.

Id_BattleText.simple: Change this to choose the description shown in battle for this effect on a binding vow.
Id_BattleText.technical: FName key supplied to SetTextIdWithParameters. UGameVsEnemyBindingVowsSelectWidget::OnVowFocused requires the vow to have at least two effect IDs, resolves effect [0] as the debuff and [1] as the buff, requires each effect's EffectValue.Num()>=2, passes [0] as VALUE and [1] as VALUE2, and then calls SetTextIdWithParameters with that effect's Id_BattleText; a failed lookup or short array collapses the corresponding text. No other direct reader of this property was identified in the reconstructed source. All 239 exported rows have non-empty BTL_BINDING_VOWS_* keys, and all of them resolve in each of the 11 exported BattleText locale tables.

notes: AGameDataTableManager::Tick resolves the registered BindingVowsEffectDataTable loader into BindingVowsEffectDataTables (Source/Abrams/Private/GameDataTableManager.cpp:168, Source/Abrams/Private/GameDataTableManager.cpp:291, Source/Abrams/Public/GameDataTableManager.h:202). No separate effect-name cache was identified; consumers use that loaded-table array plus transient row-pointer arrays.

Lookup precedence is two-level: GameBindingVows_GetEffectRows uses the first BindingVowsDataTables entry containing the vow ID, skips None effect IDs, and takes the first hit in BindingVowsEffectDataTables for each ID; DTM_FindBindingVowsEffectRow uses the same first-table rule. GetEffectRowsOfType preserves vow-ID/effect order while filtering by EffectType.

EffectValue is not a generic scalar list. Rate helpers subtract 1 from raw [0]/[1] multipliers, SumEffectValue uses raw [0], RollChance uses int32([0]*100) out of 100, and flag-only types act by EffectType presence. Empty/unused value slots are commonly 0.0; negative values are meaningful penalties in types such as ForceGaugeMax and CursedEnergyLevelMax.

Battle-log requirements are mapped by reconstructed enum values: 0x37 CursedEnergy_LevelUp, 0x32 Jump, 0x33 Step, 0x2F Guard (send/receive selected by the second argument), 0x21 SpecialTagCombo_Count, 0x20 TimeLimit and 0x47 BindingVowsPenalty. IsBindingVowsEffectMet requires Required>=0 and Current>=Required. DeadKillWithTime and DeadCursedEnergyLevelWithTime add a second EffectValue[1] check after the time requirement.

The first/second vow effect-slot convention is explicit in the selection UI's debuff/buff text and in the icon widget's category textures; all 146 exported BindingVows rows contain exactly two resolvable effect IDs. All 239 effect rows have two values and resolvable battle-text IDs in all 11 BattleText locale exports. The export covers 76 of the 80 non-None effect types; 38 effect rows are not directly referenced by the BindingVows export, and HitPointWhenKill, DashGaugeUnlimited, SendGuardDurabilityDamageAlly and DeadSendGuard are handled in C++ but have no rows in this shard.

Elapsed-time comparisons use the battle manager's GetBattleElapsedTime and the battle-log TimeLimit value; the exported 45-100 values are consistent with seconds, but the time unit is inferred from those names and data rather than independently pinned.

An unrelated structure, EquipmentItemEffect, has fields with the same names; the GameItemDescriptionTextWidget.cpp hits for EffectValue/Id_BattleText are for that type and are deliberately not used as evidence here.

Direct field reads were found in GameCharacterStatusController.cpp, GameBindingVowsWidget.cpp, GameVsEnemyBindingVowsSelectWidget.cpp, GamePhase_IntervalPvE.cpp and GamePvESettings.cpp. Indirect consumers include GameBattleSystems_B (dead-vow failure), GameCharacter/GameCharacterAction (Has*Effect), GamePhase_BattlePvEBase, GamePhase_BattlePvESolo and GamePhase_BattlePvETag (force gauge, costs and rewards).

Reconstructed static C++ plus the supplied JSON exports is the evidence base. Retail Blueprint or other uncooked consumers were not available, so this is not proof that the consumer list is exhaustive in the retail build.

usages.detail: Load/registry path: Tick resolves BindingVowsEffectDataTable into the BindingVowsEffectDataTables lookup array.
GameBindingVows_GetEffectRows joins vow IDs to these rows, skipping None IDs and taking the first vow-table and effect-table matches.
GameBindingVows_GetEffectRowsOfType filters joined rows by EffectType for status queries and UI records.
GetBindingVowsRecords builds current/required battle-log progress from EffectType and EffectValue[0], retaining the source row pointer in each state.
GameBindingVows_SumEffectValue sums raw EffectValue[0], or takes a zero-floored max when requested.
GameBindingVows_SumEffectRate accumulates EffectValue[0]-1 over matching rows (or the zero-floored max of that delta).
GameBindingVows_SumEffectRateAtValue uses EffectValue[0] as a comparison threshold and EffectValue[1]-1 as the rate contribution.
ForceGaugeMax sums EffectValue[0] over active vows; nonnegative bases are clamped to at least 1 while negative bases pass through.
ApplyJustGuardHitPointGain rolls EffectValue[0]*100 and then adds HitPointMax*EffectValue[1] for HitPointWhenJustGuard.
HitPointOnce fires at most once per effect slot when the current-HP ratio is at or below EffectValue[0], adding int32(EffectValue[1]*HitPointMax).
Dead-vow types consume the stored current/required state and, for two types, EffectValue[1] before applying the fatal binding-vow penalty.
BindingVows_GetCategoryType maps EffectType, together with the debuff/buff slot flag, to the vow icon's hit-point/movement/attack/cursed-energy/other category.
OnVowFocused formats the two vow slots' descriptions with Id_BattleText and both EffectValue parameters.
PvE mission vow selection excludes candidates whose effect types appear in mission-order or mission-task exclusion lists.
PvE setup reads HitPointMaxRate, HitPointMaxRateAlly, HitPointMax, CursedEnergyLevelMax and ForceGaugeMax rows when calculating initial stats.
Mission-clear and mission-failure reward rates consume the effect helpers indirectly through the selected vow ID lists.
